title: How we separate AI interpretation from world state in our text RPG
author: melty_program
selftext:
We're the team developing melt hollow, a browser fantasy RPG where players type their dialogue and actions.



One design choice has been to separate interpreting an action from committing its result. The model reads what a player means and proposes an outcome; game code checks that outcome against the world's rules before changing the saved state. AI also generates character dialogue and narration.



That boundary matters when several people share a quest. A convincing sentence alone shouldn't grant an item or change the outcome for everyone. The difficult part we're working on is making a rejected or limited action understandable without taking away the appeal of writing your own approach.



The current build is playable at [https://playmelt.com/](https://playmelt.com/) — English and Japanese, with Google sign-in required. It uses AI-generated text and artwork.



For others building games around free-text actions: how do you explain what an action couldn't do while keeping the response in character?
